description: The hand-verified expected result for the negative opengrep SARIF fixture whose URI references carry MALFORMED percent escapes -- a '%' that is not the start of a two-hexadecimal-digit triplet. It is the sibling of expected/reject-sarif-percent-encoded-control.rows.json and the two are deliberately the same shape over the same six captured records, because together they separate the two halves of one guard: that file's references are well-formed escapes that DECODE to something inadmissible, and this file's references are not escapes at all, so there is nothing to decode and the refusal has to happen before the decode is attempted. Every value here was derived by reading the fixture, the pinned tree and the authored contracts in harness/lib/normalize/. Where this file and harness/lib/normalize/paths.py disagree, the disagreement is the finding: diagnose it rather than overwriting this file to match. Key names follow the template expected/reject-sarif-percent-encoded-control.rows.json established, with pre_decode_validation in place of its post_decode_validation because the moment at which the fault is detected -- before the decode rather than after it -- is the whole subject of this fixture.
resolver: harness/lib/normalize/paths.py -- parse_uri_reference, describe_malformed_percent_escapes, _malformed_percent_refusal, resolve_uri_base and resolve_sarif_location. The adapter contributes nothing to this condition beyond passing the artifactLocation through and returning the rejection paths.py composed.

fixture.derivation: Derived from the sibling percent-encoded-control fixture by replacing four artifactLocation values and one uriBaseId, and nothing else. The envelope, the invocations array and all three driver rules are byte-identical to that fixture's, which makes the two directly comparable: the only difference between a well-formed escape that decodes to a control and a malformed escape that decodes to nothing is the reference itself. Through that sibling the six records are captured opengrep records from harness/artifacts/raw/opengrep.sarif, three descriptors used twice each: /runs/0/results/0 and /runs/0/results/3 carry the descriptors of raw results[429] (DiskStore.scala:72, the tainted-sql-string rule), /runs/0/results/1 and /runs/0/results/4 those of raw results[518] (test_legacy_mode_feature.py:90, avoid-pickle), and /runs/0/results/2 and /runs/0/results/5 those of raw results[1255] (ProxyUtils.java:75, url-rewriting). /runs/0/results/0 is byte-identical to raw results[429]; the other five differ from their raw counterpart in their artifactLocation object alone, every other member -- fingerprints, message, properties, ruleId, and the region with its snippet -- carried over verbatim. The reuse of descriptors is stated here rather than disguised by editing a fingerprint into something that would look captured and would not be; the adapter reads no fingerprint. The three driver rules are raw rules[592], rules[1283] and rules[1458], byte-identical. The originalUriBaseIds map carries three entries: %PROJECTROOT% and %SRCROOT% are the sibling's, verbatim, and %PCTROOT% is this fixture's one new base.
fixture.index_convention: Every raw_artifact_result_index and raw_artifact_rule_index in this file is a ZERO-BASED index into harness/artifacts/raw/opengrep.sarif's runs[0].results and runs[0].tool.driver.rules arrays, which hold 1319 and 1500 elements. The convention is stated because it is not self-evident from a number, and because the sibling expected/reject-sarif-percent-encoded-control.rows.json records 432, 521 and 1258 for the same three records where a zero-based index gives 429, 518 and 1255 -- a three-element offset in that file's derivation prose, reported rather than propagated. No test asserts either set of figures; both files' assertions run against the fixture.
fixture.provenance_verification: Reproducible without this file: parse the fixture and harness/artifacts/raw/opengrep.sarif, blank each record's artifactLocation object on both sides, and compare json.dumps(record, sort_keys=True). Each of the six matches exactly one raw record -- 429, 518, 1255, 429, 518, 1255 in fixture order -- and result 0 matches without blanking anything. Separately, json.dumps of the fixture's version, $schema, runs[0].invocations and runs[0].tool all equal the sibling fixture's, and the five changed artifactLocation objects are the whole of the difference between the two documents.
fixture.why_each_alteration_is_the_minimum: The condition under test is a malformed percent escape in a URI reference, and a URI reference is exactly what an artifactLocation carries. Four references express the fault at four different places -- a relative reference, a file: URI's path, the very end of an archive member, and a base-map entry's own uri -- and the fifth alteration is the control: a WELL-FORMED escape on the same document, which must still decode and still become a row. Changing anything else would put content in the fixture that no producer wrote, for no gain.
fixture.carries_no_control_character_note: Verified by reading the fixture as bytes: every byte is 0x09, 0x0A or >= 0x20. That matters because it separates this fixture from its sibling in the other direction too -- neither fixture's refusals come from the pre-decode CONTROL check, and this fixture's come from the pre-decode PERCENT check, which is a different guard on the same line of defence.

pre_decode_validation.why_this_fixture_exists: To assert that percent SYNTAX is validated before any decode is attempted (SEC-06). RFC 3986 section 2.1 admits '%' in a URI reference only as the start of a two-hexadecimal-digit escape. urllib.parse.unquote is documented to leave an invalid escape IN PLACE rather than raise, so '%', '%2' and '%GG' decode to themselves and then pass every downstream test there is: the value is a non-empty string, it carries no control character, it relativizes against the scan root, and it matches an allowlist glob. The result is a path column entry that is not a path, emitted with in_scope true and indistinguishable in findings.json from a real file.
pre_decode_validation.the_check_the_fixture_defeats: A control-character guard alone. Each of the four defective references passes both halves of that guard -- it carries no control as written and decodes to no control, because it does not decode at all -- so before this remediation all four produced rows. The QA reproduction is exactly that: %, %2 and %GG returned form 'relative' from parse_uri_reference and reached the dataset, one of them with in_scope true, while %00 was correctly refused.

the_two_fault_kinds.truncated: '%' is followed by fewer than two characters -- the reference was cut short, so the two digits an escape needs are simply not there. /runs/0/results/3 is this kind, and it places the '%' at the very last character of the reference, which is the position an implementation using a fixed three-character slice is most likely to read past.
the_two_fault_kinds.non_hex: '%' is not followed by two hexadecimal digits -- two characters follow, and they are not hexadecimal digits. This is the producer that meant a literal per-cent sign and failed to encode it as %25. /runs/0/results/1, /runs/0/results/2 and the %PCTROOT% base entry are this kind.
the_two_fault_kinds.why_they_are_reported_separately: They are two different producer mistakes and a reader acts on them differently: a truncated reference suggests a value that was cut, and a non-hex one suggests text that was never encoded. Naming which of the two is what makes the detail worth retaining under AAP 0.5.4 rather than a class label repeated four times.

pre_decode_validation.guard_sites: parse_uri_reference validates the whole raw reference at its head, and then validates each component again immediately before that component's own unquote -- the archive container and member behind a scheme, the file: URI's path component, and the archive container and member with no scheme. Every component decoded in that function is a substring of the raw reference, so the first check is already sufficient; the repeats exist so each decode's guard is verifiable at the point it matters rather than only by following a recursion, which is the same discipline the control guard follows.
pre_decode_validation.ordering_against_the_control_guard: Percent syntax first, control characters second, and the order is what preserves the behaviour that was already correct. %00 is a perfectly well-formed escape, so it passes the syntax check and is refused a moment later on its decoded NUL, with the control-character detail unchanged -- which is why the sibling fixture's four expected details still read 'decodes to a value that carries the control character'. Only the escapes that are not escapes are the new refusal.
pre_decode_validation.what_is_deliberately_still_accepted: A well-formed escape, whatever it encodes into a legal path character. %55 is 'U', %20 is a space, %2F is '/' and %2E%2E is '..'; a guard that refused every '%' would satisfy all four rejection assertions in this file and would be wrong. /runs/0/results/5 is the control record for exactly that, on this same document.
pre_decode_validation.identifiers_are_not_references: Every uriBaseId in this fixture is percent-wrapped -- %SRCROOT%, %PROJECTROOT%, %PCTROOT% -- and as a URI reference each one is a malformed escape. They are mapping KEYS rather than URI references and no call site passes one to parse_uri_reference, which is why the two surviving rows resolve through %SRCROOT% -> %PROJECTROOT% normally. The fixture carries them on purpose: a percent guard applied to an identifier would break SARIF path resolution outright, and it would break it silently -- every based reference would become invalid_uri and the dataset would lose the rows rather than gain an error.

routing.detected_by: normalize.shape.is_sarif -- a version of "2.1.0" together with a runs array; those two together are the whole test
routing.routing_decision: normalize.shape.route("opengrep", doc) returns tool "opengrep", shape "sarif", adapter "sarif", scanner_class "sast"
routing.not_a_shape_failure: No normalize.shape.UnknownArtifactShape is expected here. The document is valid SARIF 2.1.0 and routes cleanly; four records inside it name locations that are not URI references, and the adapter rejects those four while still emitting the other two. The fixtures that own shape-detection failure are near-sarif-version-only.json, near-sarif-runs-only.json and unknown-shape.json.

field_order_authority: harness/lib/normalize/emit.py, the FIELDS constant. Every row below carries all twelve keys in that order, present-with-null rather than omitted.
absence_convention: Absence is JSON null here and in findings.json, and an empty field in findings.csv. tool, scanner_class, rule_id, message, severity_norm, path and in_scope are never absent -- exactly emit.REQUIRED_FIELDS.

allowlist.note: in_scope is decided by that file alone. The globs are not copied here: the allowlist is the single authority and stays byte-exact. The glob each row matched is recorded per row under row_derivations.

resolution_context.path_base_source: harness/artifacts/logs/runner-metadata.json, the opengrep entry's path_base -- read as input, never assumed
resolution_context.path_basis_authority: harness/lib/normalize/paths.py, BASIS_SARIF_BASE_CHAIN. Both surviving rows resolve through the map's own chain, so the basis is the walk completing on its own evidence rather than the runner-recorded fallback.

walk_outcomes_per_base.%PROJECTROOT%: resolved -- base /opt, the absolute ancestor the other two are expressed beneath
walk_outcomes_per_base.%PCTROOT%: invalid-uri -- its own uri 'spark-src%GG/' carries a malformed percent escape at index 9, so the walk stops on its first link and no base is produced

resolution_context.walk_is_a_chain_not_one_level: Both surviving rows resolve through two links: %SRCROOT% carries uri "spark-src/" and uriBaseId %PROJECTROOT%, and %PROJECTROOT% carries the absolute file:///opt/, so the relative level is accumulated and joined beneath the absolute ancestor to give /opt/spark-src. That is SARIF 2.1.0 section 3.14.14's own shape, in which one base is expressed relative to another. %PCTROOT% is built the same way on purpose -- one relative level over the same absolute ancestor -- so that the only thing separating it from %SRCROOT% is the malformed escape in its own uri.
resolution_context.why_pctroot_is_invalid_uri_and_not_degen: paths.resolve_uri_base classifies a base entry by the form parse_uri_reference gives its uri. A form of invalid yields BASE_OUTCOME_INVALID_URI, which resolve_sarif_location rejects outright under invalid_uri; a base that is well-formed but useless -- a foreign scheme, an archive member, the filesystem root -- yields BASE_OUTCOME_DEGENERATE and is eligible for the runner-recorded fallback. The distinction matters here and is the reason result 4 is rejected even though the runner metadata does record an explicit base for opengrep: a base whose own uri is not a URI reference is not a degenerate base to fall back from, it is a malformed one, and AAP 0.5.4's fallback is not a catch-all.
resolution_context.root_dependence: The surviving rows are root-dependent, and the precondition is stated rather than glossed. The chain reconstructs the absolute directory /opt/spark-src, which is the scan root harness/artifacts/logs/runner-metadata.json records, so joining onto it and relativizing back returns each uri unchanged -- for row 1, unchanged after %55 decodes to 'U' -- and both rows name a tree_file inside the twelve globs. Given some other root the same two records resolve to ../-prefixed outside_root coordinates and are kept with in_scope false: kept and counted, never rejected.
resolution_context.rejections_are_root_independent: None of the four rejections depends on the root or on the metadata. Results 1, 2 and 3 are refused inside parse_uri_reference, which is given no root and no base at all; result 4 is refused by the base walk, which reads only the map. All four therefore carry the same class, the same detail and the same record_identity under any root and under any path_base kind, which is why this fixture's outcome is recorded once rather than as two branches.
resolution_context.severity_source: No result in this fixture states a level, and no rule states properties.severity or properties.problem.severity, so both emitted rows record no native severity at all. The rules do carry defaultConfiguration.level, and it is deliberately not consulted: AAP 0.5.4 fixes the three sources, and a rule's default configuration is the level the rule would have had rather than the level this result was reported at. severity_norm is Info with the absence stated, never a level assumed.
resolution_context.cwe_and_cve: Each emitted row's CWE comes from its rule's properties.tags, whose first entry is a 'CWE-<digits>: <name>' string; the identifier is the token, and the prose after the colon is not part of it. Neither rule carries a CVE-shaped string, and neither carries more than one CWE identifier, so no multi-valued selection is exercised here.
resolution_context.package_coordinate: null on both rows. A SARIF result names a code location rather than a package, and this shape supplies no coordinate to carry.
resolution_context.start_line: Present on every record, as an integer, in the region of the first location -- including on the four rejected ones, which is what makes their rejection specifically about the path.

rejection_boundary.statement: A reference carrying a '%' that is not the start of a two-hexadecimal-digit escape is not a URI reference, and is a rejection. A reference whose escapes are well formed is a row, whatever they encode: percent-encoding is not by itself suspicious, and the four defective records are refused for their SYNTAX rather than for being encoded.
rejection_boundary.why_it_can_only_be_a_rejection: path is one of emit.REQUIRED_FIELDS, so the row must carry one, and the only candidate these records offer is text that is not a path. Emitting it would put a non-path in the dataset with an in_scope verdict computed from it; repairing it would require choosing between two guesses -- that the producer meant %25, or that the escape's digits were lost -- and AAP 0.5.4 forbids inferring a field. Counting the record under invalid_uri is the only outcome that neither drops it nor invents a path for it.

not_a_rejection.expected: a kept row whose path carries the decoded character
not_a_rejection.evidence: /runs/0/results/5 is exactly this case, on this same document: %55 decodes to 'U' and the row's path is the real resource-managers/yarn/.../ProxyUtils.java. It is the last element of the results array, so it also carries the partial-parse proof -- a run that refused every '%' or abandoned the artifact at the first fault could not have produced it.

not_a_rejection.expected: resolved as a mapping key, exactly as before
not_a_rejection.evidence: Both rows resolve through %SRCROOT% -> %PROJECTROOT%, and %SRCROOT% is a malformed escape read as a URI reference. That the rows exist at all is the assertion.

not_a_rejection.case: a well-formed escape that decodes to a control character
not_a_rejection.expected: a rejection, but under the control-character detail rather than this one
not_a_rejection.evidence: Not present here by design; owned by reject-sarif-percent-encoded-control.sarif. Named because the two conditions must stay distinguishable in the record: a reader needs to tell a producer that emitted a broken escape from one that emitted a hostile well-formed escape.

not_a_rejection.case: a reference beginning with exactly one slash
not_a_rejection.expected: not rejected as absolute -- the SARIF 2.1.0 errata issue 480 shape
not_a_rejection.evidence: Untouched by this fixture and owned by ErrataConformanceTests. Named because the guard added here sits at the head of the same function, and a percent check that also began refusing the errata shape would be a regression this file's rows could not see.

rejection_boundary.document_versus_record_scope: This document parses. Four records inside it are self-defeating, not the file's shape, so the outcome is four per-record rejections and a partial parse rather than a halt.

counts.raw_count_unit: one element of runs[].results[] -- the unit normalize.reconcile.count_records walks independently of row construction
counts.raw_count_authority: normalize.reconcile.count_records("opengrep", doc), whose SARIF traversal sums the length of each run's results array and builds no row, resolves no path and maps no severity. It is the independent half of the identity: a count taken from the traversal that builds the rows would satisfy the assertion while testing nothing.

four_reported_counters.authority: AAP 0.5.4 -- the four counts reported per tool
four_reported_counters.note: Named here rather than restated with their values. The counters block below is the single measurement, and a number carried twice inside one document is a number that can drift; counters_note gives the reason each of the four is zero -- including why non_filesystem_paths is zero despite the fixture carrying an archive reference.

counts.parse_status_authority: harness/lib/normalize/cli.py, PARSE_STATUS_PARTIAL = "partial", assigned where there are rejections and clean where there are none. Partial is right precisely because the adapter did not abandon the artifact: every parsable record was emitted and each rejected record is counted under its class, with its reason retained.

counters_authority: harness/lib/normalize/adapters/sarif.py, COUNTER_KEYS as returned by new_counters(): nineteen authored keys, one path_kind_* per normalize.paths.PATH_KINDS member and one severity_basis_* per normalize.severity.BASIS_VALUES member, twenty-eight in total.
counters_note: Four things a reader must not "correct", and every one of them is identical to the sibling percent-encoded-control fixture's, because the two documents differ only in why their four defective references are refused. First, rule_id_from_rule_id is 6 rather than 2: the rule identifier is step 2 and the path is step 4, so all six records resolve an identifier and four of them are then refused for their path. Second, path_kind_archive_member is 0 even though result 3 carries an archive reference -- the reference is refused at the head of parse_uri_reference, before the archive branch is reached and long before archive_member_path could serialize anything, so no path kind is ever assigned to it, and non_filesystem_paths is 0 for the same reason. Third, the severity and path counters total 2 because only the two emitted records reach steps 4 and 5. Fourth, severity_absent is 2 and severity_basis_no_vocabulary is 2 rather than either being 0: both rows state no severity anywhere the adapter is authorised to look, and the absence is recorded rather than filled in from defaultConfiguration.level.

corroboration.note: Both emitted rows carry captured descriptors, so each has a counterpart in the dataset -- the opengrep rows for DiskStore.scala:72 and ProxyUtils.java:75 -- and all twelve fields of both agree. They also agree field for field with expected/reject-sarif-percent-encoded-control.rows.json and expected/reject-sarif-uribaseid-invalid-uri.rows.json, which carry the same two captured records under different base maps; row 1 agrees after %55 decodes, which is the point of writing the reference that way rather than plainly. Recorded after the fact rather than as the source of these values. Separately measured: no path field in the whole committed dataset contains a '%' in any form, so this guard changes no committed row and re-normalizing harness/artifacts/raw/ reproduces findings.json and findings.csv byte-identically.

rows.message: User data flows into this manually-constructed SQL string. User data can be safely inserted into SQL strings using prepared statements or an object-relational mapper (ORM). Manually-constructed SQL strings is a possible indicator of SQL injection, which could let an attacker steal or manipulate data from the database. Instead, use prepared statements (`connection.PreparedStatement`) or a safe library.
URL rewriting has significant security risks. Since session ID appears in the URL, it may be easily seen by third parties.

rows_note: Two rows, listed in full rather than referred to, and their positions carry the partial-parse proof: one comes from the first record in the array and one from the last, with all four rejections between them. Row 1 additionally carries the well-formed-escape proof, because its reference reaches that path only by decoding %55.

rejections.locator_note: The pointer and the run_index / result_index pair name the same record. Both are carried because paths.resolve_sarif_location is given exactly run_index, result_index and rule_id as the record identity and then adds the uri and the uriBaseId itself, so a produced Rejection's record_identity and this expectation compare directly.
rejections.decode_site: the head of parse_uri_reference, on the whole raw reference, before the relative-or-absolute branch its form would have taken
rejections.reject_class_authority: harness/lib/normalize/paths.py, the REJECT_INVALID_URI constant -- a literal member of paths.REJECT_CLASSES, the closed set of ten, whose value is the string invalid_uri. Written verbatim rather than paraphrased, and asserted against the module rather than by eye.
rejections.classification_step: step 4 of the adapter's fixed classification order -- shape, rule identifier, message, path, start_line. Steps 1 to 3 pass: the element is an object, its ruleId resolves, its message.text is present. Step 5 is never reached.
rejections.raw_reference_note: For rejections 0 to 2 this is the record's own uri, which is what failed. For rejection 3 it is the %PCTROOT% base entry's uri: the record's own uri is clean, and quoting it here would name the wrong value.
rejections.malformed_escape_fault: '%' is not followed by two hexadecimal digits
rejections.what_it_would_have_been_before_the_guard: form 'relative' with value equal to the reference itself, a tree_file path matching the glob python/pyspark/**, and a row with in_scope true. This is the QA reproduction's in_scope-true case.
rejections.expected_detail: the uri str from uri (length 62, sha256 9323e7a66b1dd8e10d40458b458ebfb38b38f32621a815ac40dd59e7b2f99769, <redacted-artifact-text>) is not a valid URI reference: the URI reference carries the malformed percent escape at index 56, where '%' is not followed by two hexadecimal digits; RFC 3986 section 2.1 admits '%' only as the start of a two-hexadecimal-digit escape, and urllib.parse.unquote leaves a malformed escape in place rather than raising, so a reference carrying one would reach the path column as text that is not a path
rejections.expected_detail_note: Retained verbatim, as AAP 0.5.4 requires of every rejection's parser reason. The detail has two halves and both are load-bearing. The leading clause identifies the value WITHOUT publishing it -- its Python type, the field it came from, the whole value's character length, the whole value's 64-hex sha256 and the fixed paths.REDACTED_TEXT marker -- because a detail is written verbatim into harness/artifacts/logs/ and normalize-run.json, and an artifact that placed a credential in a uri would otherwise have it persisted in cleartext by the very channel that refused the record (SEC-04). The length and the digest are of the whole original, so this record stays measurable and identifiable against the artifact without copying it. The sub-reason after the colon names the fault by position and by kind, which is what distinguishes this record from its three siblings under the same class.
distinguishing_substrings: '%' is not followed by two hexadecimal digits
rejections.distinguishing_substrings_note: The fault kind and the position, which together are the whole diagnosis. Neither quotes the reference.
rejections.expected_detail_must_not_contain_note: The whole raw reference always, and the offending sequence itself wherever it is more than one character. The first pins the SEC-04 redaction: a regression that restored the {uri!r} interpolation would fail here. The second pins the describer's own discipline -- it reports where the fault is and which kind it is, and never reproduces the characters, because a hex position can hold any byte at all. The sequence asserted absent for this record is the three characters at the fault index.
rejections.record_identity_note: Five keys: the three the resolver is given -- run_index, result_index and rule_id -- plus the uri and the uriBaseId it adds itself.
rejections.record_identity_carries_the_raw_uri: It does, and deliberately: the identity is the coordinate set that locates the record in the artifact, it is what a reader uses to find the record again, and paths.py sanitises it through sanitise_persisted rather than redacting it. The SEC-04 redaction applies to the composed DETAIL, whose subject is a value that failed validation. Recorded here so the distinction is explicit rather than looking like an oversight.
rejections.why_not_a_row: The reference is not a URI reference, so there is no path to put in the row, and path is never absent from a row. unquote would have returned the text unchanged, which is what made the defect invisible: the row would have looked like every other python/pyspark row in the dataset.

The leading clause identifies the value WITHOUT publishing it -- its Python type, the field it came from, the whole value's character length, the whole value's 64-hex sha256 and the fixed paths.REDACTED_TEXT marker -- because a detail is written verbatim into harness/artifacts/logs/ and normalize-run.json, and an artifact that placed a credential in a uri would otherwise have it persisted in cleartext by the very channel that refused the record (SEC-04). The length and the digest are of the whole original, so this record stays measurable and identifiable against the artifact without copying it. The sub-reason after the colon names the fault by position and by kind, which is what distinguishes this record from its three siblings under the same class.

rejections.expected_detail_must_not_contain_note: The whole raw reference always, and the offending sequence itself wherever it is more than one character. The first pins the SEC-04 redaction: a regression that restored the {uri!r} interpolation would fail here. The second pins the describer's own discipline -- it reports where the fault is and which kind it is, and never reproduces the characters, because a hex position can hold any byte at all. The sequence asserted absent for this record is the three characters at the fault index.
rejections.record_identity_note: Four keys: this record states no uriBaseId, so the resolver adds the uri alone. An absolute file: reference needs no base.
rejections.record_identity_carries_the_raw_uri: It does, and deliberately: the identity is the coordinate set that locates the record in the artifact, it is what a reader uses to find the record again, and paths.py sanitises it through sanitise_persisted rather than redacting it. The SEC-04 redaction applies to the composed DETAIL, whose subject is a value that failed validation. Recorded here so the distinction is explicit rather than looking like an oversight.
rejections.why_not_a_row: Same reason, reached through a different form. It is recorded separately because the file: branch decodes only the path component after urlsplit has parsed the reference, so a guard placed on the general decode alone would leave this route open.

prohibitions_observed.no_secret_value: No field in this file carries a secret, a credential or a token. The fixture is opengrep SAST output over source locations and contains none; each rejection carries indices, a rule identifier and the reference that made the record defective, and no record content beyond it.
prohibitions_observed.no_cross_tool_interpretation: One tool is named in each row's tool field. opengrep is this fixture's producer because the condition is a property of the shared SARIF resolver and one producer's shape exercises it -- not a statement about what any tool found, and not a comparison.
prohibitions_observed.no_deduplication: Nothing here is merged. Six records in, two rows and four rejections out, including three pairs that share a rule and a message.
prohibitions_observed.no_judgement: Neither emitted row is characterised as real, important, a false positive or a duplicate, and the four rejected records are not characterised as defects in the tool: every malformed escape in this fixture is its own edit, and the artifact they were derived from carries none -- measured, no uri in harness/artifacts/raw/opengrep.sarif carries a '%' at all.
